chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to me, saying: Al-Mu'adhi narrated to me, from Mu'mar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him),
he said: I said to him: What do the people narrate regarding mud and the dislike of it? He said: That is only with regard to the moistened [mud], and that is the clay [used for prostration].

key_terms.الطِّين: Mud, generally referring to earth mixed with water, often discussed in the context of ritual purity and prostration.
key_terms.الْمَبْلُولُ: The moistened/wet one, referring to mud that has been wetted, which is the subject of the reported dislike.
key_terms.الْمُدَرُّ: Clay or dried earth, specifically referring to the type of earth used for prostration that is distinct from wet mud.
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَتِهِ: The dislike or aversion, referring to the juristic status of makruh (disliked) rather than haram (forbidden).

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between moistened mud and clay regarding prostration in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifying the juristic distinction between 'moistened mud' (al-muballal), which may carry impurity or instability, and 'clay' (al-mudar), the dry, pure earth traditionally used for prostration. This distinction resolves the apparent contradiction in popular reports by specifying that the dislike applies only to the former, thereby affirming the permissibility of using standard clay for sujah. The narration highlights the Shia emphasis on precise material conditions for acts of worship, ensuring both physical purity and ritual validity.
